original_question: Define Donaldson-Thomas invariants for varieties of dimension greater than 3 by providing a mathematically sound framework that extends the 3-fold theory.
target_in_paper: Section (iii), “On the moduli of sheaves,” specifically Q5: “Define Donaldson–Thomas invariants in dimensions > 3.” The immediately preceding context explains that the intended issue is to extend the 3-fold moduli-of-sheaves theory, where a virtual fundamental class is used and where deformations are governed by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and one needs, roughly, Ext^i(E,E)=0 for i>2. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main target almost exactly: it asks for a definition of Donaldson–Thomas invariants beyond dimension 3, which is precisely Q5, and its reference to extending the 3-fold theory matches the surrounding explanation that the problem is the failure of the usual 3-fold virtual-fundamental-class formalism for moduli of sheaves in higher dimension. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s question is located specifically in section (iii), “On the moduli of sheaves”; it is not framed as an abstract problem about arbitrary higher-dimensional varieties independent of sheaf-moduli theory. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The nearby context says why dimension 3 is special: Donaldson–Thomas invariants there are defined using a virtual fundamental class on the moduli space of sheaves. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The paper makes the deformation-obstruction package explicit: deformations are Ext^1(E,E), obstructions are Ext^2(E,E), and one needs, roughly, Ext^i(E,E)=0 for i>2 in order to define the usual virtual fundamental class. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The “3-fold theory” in the nearby discussion means the theory defined via moduli of ideal sheaves of curves on a nonsingular projective 3-fold, and, more recently, via moduli spaces of stable pairs; the draft does not say this. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The local geometric setup just before Q5 uses a nonsingular, projective 3-fold X; a stand-alone version should retain the smooth/projective sheaf-moduli setting, but Q5 itself does not impose extra hypotheses such as Calabi–Yau, fixed Chern character, or a chosen stability condition. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

If one wants an ambient field, section (i) explicitly works over C, but section (iii) does not restate the field, so adding “over C” is an extrapolation from the paper’s general ambient setting rather than part of Q5 itself. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

There are no paper-critical variables, degree restrictions, homogeneity conditions, nilpotency hypotheses, or “for all sufficiently large m” clauses here; the missing detail is instead the obstruction-theoretic mechanism that breaks in dimensions >3. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
refined_question: For a nonsingular projective variety X of dimension d>3, can one define Donaldson–Thomas invariants attached to moduli spaces of sheaves on X by constructing a mathematically sound replacement for the 3-fold virtual fundamental class formalism—where, for a sheaf E, infinitesimal deformations are governed by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and the usual 2-term obstruction theory fails because higher Ext^i(E,E) for i>2 need not vanish—thereby extending the dimension-3 theory defined via moduli of ideal sheaves of curves, or more recently via stable pairs? ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Q5 almost verbatim. I sharpened it only by importing the immediately adjacent information that tells us what “define Donaldson–Thomas invariants” means in this paper: one is working in the moduli-of-sheaves context, trying to reproduce the 3-fold virtual-fundamental-class package, and the core obstruction is the possible nonvanishing of Ext^i(E,E) for i>2. I did not add hypotheses such as Calabi–Yau, fixed numerical invariants, a specific stability condition, or a GW/DT correspondence, because none of those belong to Q5 as stated. The paper does not supply an explicitly equivalent reformulation of Q5, so no alternate formulation is justified. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
